title: Edge Provenance Metric Tap for Per-request Inference KPIs
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build an edge-aware Prometheus/OTel tapping component that captures per-request inference KPIs with causal provenance, and emits canonicalized metrics and deterministic identifiers for downstream SLO computation and latency/error dashboards. The tap runs as a lightweight sidecar or node-level daemon on Dedicated/Edge nodes and augments existing OTLP and Prom scrape flows without changing client libraries.
scope: Deliver a beta-quality collector that: (1) attaches stable per-request IDs to traces and metrics, (2) extracts inference-specific labels (model_id, route, slice, tenant_id, sequence_len, kv_cache_hit), (3) emits a Prom-compatible metrics stream and OTLP-enriched traces to the central telemetry fabric, and (4) provides a feature flag to enable sampling/aggregation at the edge.
decisions: Use a sidecar binary written in Go to minimize heap variability on inference processes
Generate stable request provenance using SHA256(request_id + tenant_id + node_id) truncated to 128 bits
Expose two sinks: OTLP gRPC for traces/structured metrics and a Prometheus scrape endpoint for legacy consumers
tradeoffs: Local enrichment increases CPU on edge nodes but reduces downstream ingestion volume via early aggregation
Prom scrape is simpler for dashboards but requires careful label cardinality controls
Sampling at the edge reduces cost but risks losing rare-error signals; controlled via rate-limited reservoir sampling
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar builds and runs on Dedicated/Edge node images with <3% p95 CPU overhead on our benchmark generation workload
Per-request provenance ID appears in both trace spans and metric labels for >99% of requests in functional tests
An end-to-end test validates a synthetic high-latency request surface and shows correct attribution in Grafana latency and error dashboards
Prom scrape exposes stable metric names with cardinality caps enforced; integration tests assert label set size <= configured limit
Documentation for enabling the tap and feature flag rollout is published in Confluence with a migration checklist
